opportunities.title: County Watershed and Stream Riparian Restoration Program
opportunities.summary: Install riparian stream buffers and natural bank stabilization along Assunpink Creek to filter runoff and restore natural hydrology.
opportunities.rationale: With 66 of 70 assessed waters impaired and 50 inches of yearly precipitation, restoring buffers near Assunpink #20 Dam improves stream quality.
plan: Survey water quality parameters and bank erosion surrounding Assunpink #20 Dam.
Engage local college graduates in environmental science to finalize planting designs.
Secure necessary stream encroachment and stormwater permits from state environmental regulators.
Procure native trees and wetland vegetation suited to local wet conditions.
Coordinate county conservation crews to plant riparian vegetative buffers.
Establish ongoing stream water sampling to track bacterial and nutrient reduction.

compliance: Confirm dam maintenance compliance with the municipal owner.
Obtain state freshwater wetlands general permits.

narrative.summary: Mercer County faces impaired streams across 94.3% of assessed waters, high natural hazard risks from inland flooding and heat waves, and ozone levels exceeding federal standards. To address these vulnerabilities, the county can leverage its dense educational network, brownfields, and non-powered dams. The proposed strategy deploys watershed restoration along critical creeks, establishes emergency resilience hubs at public colleges and schools, transitions fossil turbine sites to solar, upgrades older homes, expands shaded areas, and supports compliance for affected community drinking water systems.
caveats: The opportunities were written by Gemini from the needs, factors and sites in this report. Each was checked to use only this report's needs, sites and numbers. Feasibility and cost were not checked. Course-of-action and compliance lines are planning checks, not legal advice; confirm permits and local rules with counsel and the right agencies.
Figures marked as estimates are rough. The assumptions behind each one are listed with it.
A listed funding program is a lead to check, not a finding that the county or project is eligible. Confirm status and deadlines with the agency.
